answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work, and the protocol slashes that stake when independent audits prove fraud. A crystal-clear reputation score then grows only from accepted work, so creating many identities does not multiply influence: each starts with no history and needs its own locked capital. The lantern of public audit records helps reviewers spot copied behavior, while a bridge to higher task limits opens only after costly, verified contributions. A sybil attacker must therefore fund and risk a separate stake for every identity.
